    AI Overview
    Artemis II is scheduled to splash down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California, on Friday, April 10, 2026, at approximately 8:07 p.m. ET (00:07 GMT on April 11), following a 10-day crewed lunar flyby. Recovery teams will retrieve the crew from the Orion spacecraft. 
    Key Artemis II Landing Details (April 10, 2026): 
    • Location: Pacific Ocean, off the coast of San Diego, CA.
    • Time: Approx. 8:07 p.m. EDT (17:07 PDT).
    • Coverage: NASA+ and YouTube will provide live streaming starting around 6:30 p.m. ET. 
    Future Artemis Landings (Lunar Landings): 
    • Artemis III: Planned to land astronauts on the Moon in mid-2027.
    • Artemis IV: Planned to land astronauts on the Moon in early 2028. 
    The April 10 splashdown marks the safe return of the first crewed mission to the vicinity of the Moon in over 50 years.

    Will Artemis 2 be visible from Earth?
    Artemis 2 will be visible for many U.S. observers early on Friday morning, April 10. From a Midwestern location of 40° N 90° W, it rises shortly before 1 A.M. local daylight time and is highest around 5 A.M., remaining visible through dawn and setting after sunrise.1 day ago
